issues.display_title: Issue #595: Duplicate project from the dashboard: owner-only Duplicate action wired to the new backend endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Description

There is no way to branch off an existing project from the dashboard — the only path to a variant of a venue is rebuilding the floor plan from scratch. Add a Duplicate action that forks a project into a fully independent copy, so a user can try changes or keep a snapshot without touching the published original.

The backend does the actual copying: POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate (Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#131, merged) copies the project row, every project_files row and every stored blob, and re-points the file paths baked into the stored JSON. This task is the frontend surface for it.

Scope

Server action — duplicateProject(id) in src/actions/projects.ts: POST {API}/v1/projects/{id}/duplicate, projectActionFailure on non-OK so a 403 surfaces the owner's email like the other owner-only actions, revalidatePath("/dashboard"), returns the new Project.

Dashboard menu — a Duplicate entry in the shared ActionsMenu in src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx, rendered for both ProjectTile and ProjectRow. It runs straight from the menu with no confirmation dialog: duplicating is additive, nothing is destroyed.

Owner gating — the entry goes through the existing useOwnerOnlyGuard, so a collaborator gets OwnerOnlyDialog instead of a request, exactly like publish/unpublish/delete (§A9). OwnerOnlyAction gains "duplicate" and the dialog copy is updated to name duplicating alongside the other three.

Dashboard state — handleDuplicate in src/app/dashboard/useDashboard.ts: no optimistic row (the copy's id, project_key and thumbnail are all server-minted), set actionError on failure, then refreshList() + refreshCounts() — the copy arrives as a draft, which shifts the status tab counts.

Acceptance Criteria

  • "Duplicate" appears in the "…" menu on both the Recent tiles and the All-projects rows
  • Duplicating an owned project creates a copy named "{name} - copy" that appears in the list after the refresh
  • The copy is a draft even when the original is published, and it does not carry the original's public link
  • Editing the copy in the editor never changes the original — floor images, canvas, information records and categories are all independent
  • A collaborator (non-owner) sees the entry but gets the owner-only dialog and no request is sent
  • A backend 403 surfaces the owner-naming error in the dashboard error banner
  • Status tab counts update after a duplicate
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Dependencies

Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#131 — POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate. Merged to development; must be deployed before this ships or the menu item 404s.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/595-duplicate-project, commit 6bd55f3, merged to development via PR #596 (89ed23a).

Files

  • src/actions/projects.ts — duplicateProject(id): POST {API}/v1/projects/{id}/duplicate, projectActionFailure on non-OK so a 403 carries the owner's email, revalidatePath("/dashboard"), returns the new Project.
  • src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx — Duplicate entry in the shared ActionsMenu, threaded to ProjectTile and ProjectRow through the existing Handlers type.
  • src/lib/collaboration/ownerGuard.ts — OwnerOnlyAction gains "duplicate".
  • src/components/collaboration/OwnerOnlyDialog.tsx — restriction copy now names duplicating alongside publishing, unpublishing and deleting.
  • src/app/dashboard/useDashboard.ts + src/app/dashboard/page.tsx — handleDuplicate.
  • src/app/design-preview/collaboration/CollaborationPreview.tsx — the design preview passes the new handler.
  • src/actions/__tests__/projects.test.ts — asserts the POST path and the returned draft copy, plus the shared 403 owner-details case.

Decisions

  • No confirmation dialog: duplicating is additive and destroys nothing. The owner guard still runs at the menu-item handler, before any request, so a collaborator gets OwnerOnlyDialog — the same placement the destructive entries use (§A9).
  • No optimistic row: the copy's id, project_key and thumbnail are all server-minted and it lands as a draft, which shifts the status tab counts, so the list and counts are reconciled after the call instead of guessed.
  • The copy being a draft on its own share key is enforced by the backend, not here — the original's public link is never touched.

Checks — pnpm test 896 passed / 3 skipped, pnpm lint clean, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Deploy order — Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#131 (PR #132) must be deployed before this ships, or the menu item 404s.

issues.display_title: Issue #598: Confirm before duplicating a project: add a confirmation modal to the dashboard Duplicate action
issues.main_description_html:
Description

The dashboard Duplicate action (#595) fires straight from the "…" menu with no confirmation. Every other project action in that menu — Publish, Unpublish, Delete — opens a PreviewConfirmDialog first, so Duplicate is the odd one out: a stray click silently creates a second project, and nothing tells the user what a duplicate actually produces.

Add the confirmation step and say what the copy will be.

Scope

src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx only.

  • "duplicate" joins the MenuModal union and the OWNER_ONLY list, so it routes through the existing openModal → useOwnerOnlyGuard → PreviewConfirmDialog path instead of its own bespoke handler. The owner guard still runs at the menu-item handler, before the confirm and before any request.
  • New PreviewConfirmDialog for modal === "duplicate": Copy icon, non-destructive styling (primary confirm button, not the red one — duplicating destroys nothing), confirm label "Duplicate Project", busy label "Duplicating…".
  • Confirm runs through the shared run() helper, which drives busy — so the dialog shows a spinner, disables both buttons and ignores Escape/backdrop while the request is in flight, and cannot be double-fired.
  • Copy states what the user gets: an independent copy named "{name} - copy" including floors and images, starting as a draft, and editing it never changes the original.

The bespoke local duplicate handler is removed — it existed only to skip the confirm.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Clicking Duplicate opens a confirmation modal instead of duplicating immediately
  • Cancel / Escape / backdrop closes it with nothing created
  • Confirm shows the busy state and cannot be double-fired
  • The modal names the project and states the copy is a draft that will not affect the original
  • A collaborator still gets OwnerOnlyDialog instead of the confirm, and no request is sent
  • The confirm button is the primary style, not the destructive red used by Delete
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Dependencies

Follows #595 (Duplicate action), merged to development.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/598-duplicate-confirm, commit c2088e7, merged to development via PR #599 (2aa012a).

File — src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx only (+28 −17).

What changed

  • "duplicate" added to the MenuModal union and to OWNER_ONLY, so the entry routes through the existing openModal → useOwnerOnlyGuard → PreviewConfirmDialog path instead of its own handler. The bespoke duplicate callback — which existed only to skip the confirm — is deleted.
  • New PreviewConfirmDialog for modal === "duplicate": Copy icon, primary (non-destructive) confirm button, "Duplicate Project" / "Duplicating…".
  • Confirm runs through the shared run() helper, so busy drives the spinner, disables both buttons and makes the modal ignore Escape/backdrop mid-request — no double-fire.
  • Copy names the project and states the outcome: an independent copy named "{name} - copy" including floors and images, starting as a draft, with no effect on the original.
  • Guard placement is unchanged — it still fires at the menu-item handler, before the confirm and before any request, so a collaborator gets OwnerOnlyDialog and never reaches the confirm (§A9).

Checks — pnpm test 896 passed / 3 skipped, pnpm lint clean, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #600: Scope Add Panorama import to the active building
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Add Panorama routes imported panoramas to the wrong building today. groupPanosByLevel() (src/components/editor/add-panorama/placeMarkers.ts:80) resolves a tour's floor index against floorConfigs — the project's entire floor list, across every building. With Building B selected, a tour's floor 0 still lands on the first floor of Building A.

This is a live defect, not just missing UI: it breaks R1, R2, R4, R11 and R12 of the PRD in #597 before any mapping control exists.

It leaks through both import paths, and each one calls groupPanosByLevel independently:

  • Apply Based on Location — src/components/editor/add-panorama/ApplyLocationModal.tsx:155 (builds the level tabs and the per-level alignment transforms)
  • Plain Import — src/components/editor/floorplan-editor/AddPanoramaButton.tsx:61 (commits the markers)

Because the button re-runs the routing instead of using what the modal already decided, the two can disagree. That has to be closed now, before #597's editable mapping lands on top of it — with a user-chosen mapping, a second independent router is guaranteed to diverge.

The building-scoping rule already exists and is used in eight places: levelsInBuilding(levels, buildings, selectedBuildingId) in src/lib/editor/levels.ts:114. It already implements the implicit-default-building fallback the PRD asks for in R2 (a level with no buildingId belongs to the first building record; a project with no buildings keeps every level in scope). Reuse it — do not write a second scoping rule.

Scope

  • groupPanosByLevel resolves the tour floor index against the active building's floors only, in the user-visible floorConfigs order (keep the existing floorConfigs-not-levels indexing — see the #472 note in its docstring). A pano with no floor index, or an index past the building's floor count, keeps falling back to the active level.
  • The fallback active level must itself be inside the active building. scopedActiveLevelId() (src/lib/editor/levels.ts) already answers this; the two call sites pass the store's raw activeLevelId.
  • Plain Import gets the same scoping — the PRD's UI section only names the Apply modal, but R1 scopes the whole feature.
  • ApplyLocationModal returns the routing it used — a panoId → levelId map handed out through onApply / onImported — and AddPanoramaButton consumes it instead of re-deriving. One router, one answer. This is also the seam the mapping UI plugs into.
  • No visible copy changes, no new controls. The modal's Level tabs keep working; they just stop listing other buildings' floors.

Out of scope

Deliberately left for the follow-up task: the building-name header, the floor-count summary, the per-floor dropdowns, one-to-one enforcement, and the skipped-floor warning.

Acceptance Criteria

  • With Building B selected, imported panoramas land only on Building B floors — through Apply Based on Location and through plain Import
  • Floors from other buildings never appear in the Apply modal's Level tabs
  • A project with no building records behaves exactly as it does today (implicit default building)
  • A single-floor tour still imports onto the active level with no extra steps
  • Panoramas with no tour floor index fall back to an active level inside the active building
  • AddPanoramaButton no longer calls groupPanosByLevel — it places using the map the modal returned
  • Unit tests: building-scoped index resolution, the no-buildings fallback, out-of-range index, and that the modal's routing is what actually gets committed
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Refs

PRD: #597 — docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-10-add-panorama-building-floor-mapping/prd.md on branch product-docs (R1, R2, R4, R11, R12, R14).

Repro data

Project 6397e363-8df6-479d-a42b-1894ed76bb17 ("Warung Bisnis Cuaca") on the dev backend has the shape that triggers this:

Building Floors (stored order)
gothru Floor 1, Floor 2
tetangga Floor 2, Floor 3

Project-wide floorConfigs therefore starts with gothru's floors. Select tetangga, import a 2-floor virtual tour through Add Panorama, and tour floors 0 and 1 resolve to floorConfigs[0] and floorConfigs[1] — both of which belong to gothru. The entire import lands in the wrong building.

Note the two buildings each have a floor named "Floor 2". Floor names are user labels and are not unique across buildings, so nothing in the UI or the routing can key off the name — resolution must go through the building-scoped floor list.

RESULT

Shipped in 1b6d81b, merged to development via #603 as e24d0e2.

groupPanosByLevel now scopes the tour floor index to the active building through levelsInBuilding / scopedActiveLevelId — the rule the floor picker and editor already use, which also carries the implicit-default-building fallback, so projects with no building records behave exactly as before. Both import paths route through it.

Aligned panoramas additionally carry the level their position was projected against (PlacedPosition), so the importer places them on that exact floor instead of re-deriving it. The two passes agreed only by coincidence, and a position measured in one level's coordinate space must never be written to another. Placement is now decided by one pure planPanoramaPlacements().

Files: add-panorama/placeMarkers.ts, ApplyLocationModal.tsx, AddPanoramaModal.tsx, add-panorama/types.ts, floorplan-editor/AddPanoramaButton.tsx, lib/editor/levels.ts, plus 8 new tests in __tests__/placeMarkers.test.ts.

pnpm test 904 passed / 3 skipped · pnpm lint clean · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

One AC was written wrong and is closed differently than stated: "AddPanoramaButton no longer calls groupPanosByLevel" is not achievable, because plain Import never opens the alignment modal and so has no modal routing to inherit. The intent — one routing decision, no chance of two passes disagreeing — is met by planPanoramaPlacements(), which is the only place either path decides a level.

Browser verification was deliberately skipped: the sample tour has 30 of 31 panoramas located, and Import & Apply Location commits the unlocated one before the alignment modal opens, which would write markers into a live project through the 2s autosave. Covered by unit tests instead.

issues.display_title: Issue #601: Map building floors to virtual-tour floors in Apply Based on Location
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Apply Based on Location matches a tour's floors to project floors purely by order, silently, with no way to see or change the result. groupPanosByLevel() pairs tour floor 0 with the first floor, 1 with the second, and so on. When the tour's floor order does not match the building's, panoramas land on the wrong floor and the user only finds out after the import.

Give the pairing a UI: show which building is being imported into, and let each building floor pick its virtual-tour floor.

Depends on the building-scoping task, which makes the modal the single source of routing (panoId → levelId handed to onImported). This task turns that routing from order-derived into user-chosen and renders the controls.

Scope

src/components/editor/add-panorama/ApplyLocationModal.tsx and its level-tab area.

Context header

  • Active building name, plain language: Importing into: Main Building
  • Summary line: 3 building floors, 3 virtual-tour floors detected
  • No raw ids anywhere in the UI (R16)

Mapping controls

  • One dropdown per active-building floor, each selecting one virtual-tour floor
  • Option labels use pano counts: Virtual tour floor 2 - 14 panoramas. Tour-provided floor names are not available yet — the parser drops them (see Notes), so fallback labels only for now
  • Default selection is by order, matching today's behavior: first building floor ↔ first virtual-tour floor, and so on until one list runs out. Extras stay unmapped
  • A virtual-tour floor chosen for one building floor is disabled in the others, labeled Already selected
  • Each dropdown carries a — Skip — option so a mapping can be cleared, which frees that virtual-tour floor for another dropdown
  • Helper copy: Each virtual-tour floor can be used once.
  • Warning when any virtual-tour floor is unmapped: Unmapped virtual-tour floors will not be imported. — informational, never blocking

Apply

  • Imports only panoramas whose virtual-tour floor is mapped; unmapped floors are skipped and are not dumped onto the active level as a fallback
  • Works as long as at least one floor is mapped
  • The existing per-level alignment (own dots, own links, own transform, backdrop swap) follows the mapping — retargeting a dropdown moves that group of dots to the newly selected floor
  • Existing alignment controls, per-pin drag, link lines and label toggles are unchanged

Single-floor tours (R14)

Hide the mapping block entirely when the tour has one floor or fewer — a one-row dropdown is friction with no decision behind it. The context header still shows.

Empty states

  • No virtual-tour floors detected
  • No floors in the active building

Out of scope

Remembering a mapping between imports, auto-detecting the building from the tour, and any geometry/AI floor matching — all Non-Goals in the PRD.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The modal shows the active building name and the building-floor / virtual-tour-floor counts
  • Only active-building floors appear as mapping rows
  • Every building floor has a labeled virtual-tour floor dropdown with pano counts in the options
  • The default mapping is by order and matches the pre-change routing
  • Changing a dropdown re-targets that group; the previous virtual-tour floor becomes selectable again
  • A virtual-tour floor selected once is disabled elsewhere with a visible reason
  • — Skip — clears a mapping and frees the option
  • The skip warning appears when at least one virtual-tour floor is unmapped and never blocks Apply
  • Apply imports only mapped floors; skipped panoramas are not placed anywhere
  • Apply succeeds with one floor mapped
  • A single-floor tour shows no mapping controls and imports as before
  • Both empty states render
  • No raw ids in any label, option, or helper text
  • Keyboard reaches every dropdown; each has a visible label
  • Unit tests: default order mapping, duplicate prevention, clearing frees the option, unmapped floors skipped on Apply, single-floor passthrough
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Notes

Tour-provided floor names DO exist — multiple_map_data[].title, a localized object — but parseOverlay drops them (src/lib/tourmkr/overlay.ts:147), so nothing reaches the UI yet. Surfacing them is #602. This task ships the fallback labels (Virtual tour floor N - 14 panoramas); #602 swaps in the real names behind the same label helper.

Test fixture for this task: tour tourmkr.com/F1nDp6sEYY/47632194 (2 floors, 25 + 6 panoramas) against project 6397e363-8df6-479d-a42b-1894ed76bb17, whose tetangga building also has 2 floors.

Dependencies

Follows the Add Panorama building-scoping task.

Refs

PRD: #597 — docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-10-add-panorama-building-floor-mapping/prd.md on branch product-docs (R3, R5–R10, R13, R14, R16).

RESULT

Shipped in 5fee6e6, merged to development via #605 as 7fde64c.

Apply Based on Location now shows the active building, the floor counts on both sides, and one dropdown per building floor. Default mapping stays the old order-based pairing, so a tour that already lined up behaves identically — it is just visible and editable now. One-to-one is enforced by moving a taken floor rather than refusing the click, with the option disabled elsewhere as "Already selected". — Skip — clears a row; skipped tour floors are not imported and never fall back to the active level. Apply disables only when nothing is mapped. Single-floor tours show no controls; a building with no floors gets an empty state.

Also fixed along the way: skipping the floor you were aligning used to leave the backdrop on a floor with no dots, because the selected level key was trusted after its group disappeared. It is now read back off the surviving groups.

Files: new add-panorama/floorMapping.ts (pure rules) + ApplyLocationModal.tsx, with 15 new tests in __tests__/floorMapping.test.ts.

pnpm test 919 passed / 3 skipped · pnpm lint clean · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Verified in the browser against a two-building fixture (gothru / Floor 1, tetangga / Floor 2 + Floor 3, selection on tetangga): only tetangga floors offered, counts correct, each dropdown disables the other's choice, one skip raises the warning, both skips disable Apply. Not run against a live project on purpose — Import & Apply Location commits any unlocated panorama before the modal opens, which would write markers through the 2s autosave.

Dropdown labels are the positional fallback; the tour's own floor names are #602.

issues.display_title: Issue #602: Surface virtual-tour floor names from the overlay
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

The PRD in #597 asks the virtual-tour floor dropdowns to use the tour's own floor names when it has them. It does — parseOverlay just throws them away.

For a multi-floor Floor Map tour, each widgets.map.multiple_map_data[] entry carries a localized title alongside its dots. The parser reads only dots and image (src/lib/tourmkr/overlay.ts:147), so no name ever reaches ParsedOverlay, DetectedTour, or the UI. The mapping dropdowns fall back to Virtual tour floor N for every tour, even one whose floors are named.

Confirmed against a live tour — tourmkr.com/F1nDp6sEYY/47632194, two floors:

multiple_map: true
multiple_map_data[0] = { title: {"en": "1"}, image: "...", map_angle: 0, dots: 25 }
multiple_map_data[1] = { title: {"en": "2"}, image: "...", map_angle: 0, dots: 6 }

title has the same localized shape as a dot's name, so the existing nameEn() helper in the same file reads it with no new parsing code.

Scope

  • ParsedOverlay gains the per-level names, in level-index order — index i is the same index stampLevel writes onto each record, so the dropdown labels and the pano routing stay in step.
  • parseOverlay's multiple_map_data branch fills them with nameEn(lvl.title). Single-map and Journey tours produce none.
  • Carry them through toDetectedTour onto DetectedTour, next to panoramas and links.
  • The mapping dropdown uses the name when the tour has one, keeping the Virtual tour floor N fallback when it does not and the - N panoramas count either way.

Note on the observed data: the sample tour's titles are literally "1" and "2", so a name-only label renders as 1 - 25 panoramas — thin on its own. Worth deciding during implementation whether to render the name alone or keep the positional prefix (Virtual tour floor 1 - 25 panoramas) when the title is short or purely numeric. Either is a copy decision, not a data one.

Out of scope

map_angle and the per-level image are also dropped today. Neither is needed for floor mapping — leave them.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A multi-floor tour's floor names reach DetectedTour, in level-index order matching pano.level
  • Dropdown options show the tour's floor name when present, with the pano count
  • A tour with no floor names still shows Virtual tour floor N - N panoramas
  • Single-map and Journey tours are unaffected
  • A level whose title is missing or non-English-keyed degrades to the fallback label, not to an empty option
  • Unit tests on parseOverlay for the named multi-floor case, the unnamed case, and the single-map case
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Test fixture

tourmkr.com/F1nDp6sEYY/47632194 — tour key nDp6sEYY, 2 floors, 25 and 6 panoramas. Its overlay resolves through the internal tour lookup to https://gothru.co/moderation/30552/sv_XzZduOu6wC80PSoojp/overlay/798040/overlay.json, which is fetchable without auth and can be captured as a test fixture.

Pairs with project 6397e363-8df6-479d-a42b-1894ed76bb17, whose tetangga building also has exactly two floors — a clean end-to-end manual check for the building-scoping and mapping tasks.

Dependencies

Follows the Apply Based on Location mapping UI task, which renders the labels.

Refs

PRD: #597 — docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-10-add-panorama-building-floor-mapping/prd.md on branch product-docs (§3 "Virtual-tour floor dropdown").

RESULT

Shipped in 50c0531, merged to development via #606 as 4b02f45.

ParsedOverlay.levelNames / DetectedTour.levelNames now carry multiple_map_data[].title, read with the existing nameEn() helper and indexed by the level index already stamped onto each record. The floor-mapping dropdown labels a floor with its name when it has one and falls back to Virtual tour floor N otherwise, keeping the panorama count in both. Single-map and Journey tours report no names and are unaffected.

Copy decision, which this issue left open: a title that is nothing but digits is treated as unnamed. The fixture tour names its floors "1" and "2", which rendered as 1 - 25 panoramas — checked in the browser, unreadable next to a building floor called "Floor 2", and a bare number says nothing the position does not already say. A name that merely contains a digit ("Level 2 Annex") is kept.

Files: lib/tourmkr/overlay.ts, add-panorama/processTour.ts, add-panorama/types.ts, add-panorama/floorMapping.ts, ApplyLocationModal.tsx, plus 9 new tests across overlay.test.ts and floorMapping.test.ts.

pnpm test 927 passed / 3 skipped · pnpm lint clean · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Parser tests cover the named multi-floor case, an untitled floor, a title in a language the reader does not take (empty rather than wrong), and the single-map case.

issues.display_title: Issue #607: Preview/live: Overview as a selectable mode in the building dropdown
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Overview already exists in preview/live, but only as a side effect of zooming. useAutoOutdoor (src/lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts:41) flips a component-local boolean when the camera crosses OUTDOOR_ENTER_ZOOM / OUTDOOR_EXIT_ZOOM, and PreviewOverlay hides indoor UI while it is true. There is no way for a viewer to choose it, and no way to read which mode they are in: PreviewControls (src/components/editor/preview/PreviewControls.tsx:91) hides BuildingSelector and FloorSelector entirely while outdoor, so the one control that could show the mode disappears exactly when it matters.

The result is a viewer who zoomed out and cannot get back to a named building without hunting for it with the camera.

Scope

  • BuildingSelector (src/components/editor/BuildingSelector.tsx) gains an Overview entry above the building list, in preview/live only. The editor sidebar/map usage of this component must not change.
  • Selecting Overview activates overview mode. Selecting a building exits overview and shows that building indoors — the dropdown is the mode indicator (R5).
  • The manual choice and the zoom threshold drive one state, not two. Zooming out past the threshold selects Overview in the dropdown; zooming back into a building selects that building (that transition already resolves the building via buildingIdAtLngLat). Manual selection must survive until the user's own zoom crosses a threshold — keep the existing hysteresis, do not add a second one.
  • Selecting a building from Overview moves the camera into it (reuse getBuildingLngLatBounds + the existing BUILDING_VIEW_PITCH / BUILDING_VIEW_BEARING fit), otherwise the zoom watcher immediately re-selects Overview.
  • Keep the dropdown visible while Overview is active. FloorSelector stays hidden there (R8), and floor controls stay scoped to the selected building (R26).
  • Overview must remain usable with a single building (R12) — today BuildingSelector returns null when buildings.length === 0 and disables itself at length 1; a project with one building still needs the Overview choice.
  • View-only. No add/rename/delete/placement affordance may appear (R6, R11).

Out of scope

Context shells, shell click-to-enter, cross-building directions, and the recenter button — separate tasks against the same PRD.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Preview and live building dropdowns list Overview alongside the buildings
  • Selecting Overview switches to overview mode; floors and indoor-only UI hide
  • Selecting a building exits Overview, shows that building indoors, and moves the camera to it
  • The dropdown reads Overview after a manual zoom-out crosses the threshold, and reads the building after zooming back in
  • The dropdown stays visible and correct in overview mode
  • A single-building project can still enter Overview
  • No building management control is reachable from preview or live
  • Unit tests: the mode-resolution rule (manual pick vs zoom threshold) and the dropdown option list
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Refs

PRD: #590 — docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-07-overview-recenter-map/prd.md on branch product-docs (R1–R6, R8–R12, R43–R47).
Existing behaviour: #549 (outdoor massing + auto zoom), #570 (outdoor view-only gating).

RESULT

Shipped in cdc8429, merged to development via #612 as 0a9c186.

BuildingSelector gains an Overview row whenever the caller passes overviewActive — preview/live do, the editor does not, so its dropdown is unchanged. The control stays visible in Overview and names the current mode, which is what makes it the way back into a named building.

The design decision worth recording: the zoom watcher remains the single owner of the mode. A dropdown pick moves the camera into the zoom range that means the picked mode (zoomForMode) rather than adding a second source of truth that the next zoom event would contradict. getBuildingLngLatBounds therefore learned an optional building id, so entering a building frames that building rather than the site.

Trade-off this accepts: picking Overview always lands at zoom ≤ 16.0. On a campus that is the site view the PRD wants; on a project whose buildings are tens of metres across it reads as zoomed further out than strictly needed.

Files: BuildingSelector.tsx, preview/PreviewControls.tsx, PreviewOverlay.tsx, Editor3DMapView.tsx, lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts, lib/map/geojson-utils.ts, plus 11 new tests.

pnpm test · pnpm lint · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Browser-checked on a real two-building project: Overview hides Direction/Floor and shows shells, picking a building flies in and rescopes the floor list, and a manual zoom-out moves the dropdown to Overview by itself.

Follow-up 346c429 (#616). The zoom clamp described above turned out to be wrong in practice: checked at 1080p, a project whose buildings are tens of metres across had Overview push the camera two levels further out than the site needed, leaving the buildings a speck. Overview now frames the site at whatever zoom fits and anchors the return-indoors threshold just above it. Zooming out still never leaves Overview; zooming back in past where it was framed enters the building under the camera.

issues.display_title: Issue #608: Preview/live: keep other buildings as labeled context shells, clickable to enter
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Inside a building, the rest of the project vanishes. levelsAtOrBelow (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:266) correctly scopes indoor geometry to the active building's stack (#566), and the outdoor massing layer is all-or-nothing — useOutdoorLayer (src/lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts:91) toggles visibility on every shell at once, tied to visible: outdoor. So the moment a viewer enters a building, every other building disappears instead of staying as site context.

The shells themselves are also inert: buildingIdAtLngLat is called only from the zoom transition (useOutdoorMode.ts:65). Clicking a building in overview does nothing.

Scope

  • Shell rendering takes a set of building ids instead of one boolean. Overview renders every building as a shell; indoor mode renders every building except the ones being shown indoors. The indoor set is the selected building plus, later, route/hover buildings — model it as a set now so #609 can add ids without another rewrite.
  • The shell label gains a building icon next to the name (R13). outdoorGeoJson already emits an outdoor-label feature per building (geojson-utils.ts:879) and OUTDOOR_LAYER_SPECS renders ["get","name"] (layer-definitions.ts:323).
  • A building with no name falls back to the project's building-name pattern rather than dropping its label — today the label feature is skipped entirely when building?.name is falsy (R19).
  • Clicking a shell selects that building and enters it indoors: set the selected building, set its active floor, move the camera. Reuse buildingIdAtLngLat or a maplibre queryRenderedFeatures hit on the shell layer — the shell carries buildingId in its properties already. Click beats hover: a click commits the selection.
  • Keep labels compact — they must not take over the map on a dense site.

Out of scope

Overview as a dropdown option, cross-building directions, hover/focus temporary indoor preview, recenter.

Acceptance Criteria

  • With one building selected, the other buildings render as outer shells with icon + name
  • The selected building renders indoors; no other building shows indoor detail
  • Overview still renders every building as a shell
  • Clicking a shell selects that building, activates a floor in it, and moves the camera in
  • Floor controls stay scoped to the selected building after a shell click
  • A building with no name still gets a label
  • Unit tests: the indoor-vs-shell building split, and shell geojson carrying a label for an unnamed building
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Refs

PRD: #590 — docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-07-overview-recenter-map/prd.md on branch product-docs (R13–R21, R25–R27).
Existing behaviour: #549, #566, #567 (smallest-footprint building picking), #568 (shell level).

RESULT

Shipped in 21067fb, merged to development via #613 as 4801768.

The massing layer now takes the set of buildings to draw instead of a visibility flag: Overview asks for all of them, and inside a building the viewer asks for the others so they stay as context shells. viewerBuildingSplit (src/lib/preview/viewerBuildings.ts) owns that rule, deliberately shaped as a set — #609 adds route and hover buildings to the same list.

Shell labels gained the building icon. It is drawn at runtime rather than added to a sprite: the basemap owns the sprite and replaces it whole on every vector ↔ satellite switch, so an entry of ours would not survive one. A blank building name now falls back to the same Untitled building a new building gets, and that string is shared with addBuilding instead of duplicated.

Clicking a shell selects the building, re-points the floor and flies in — the same path the dropdown takes, so click and dropdown can never disagree.

Files: lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts, lib/map/geojson-utils.ts, lib/map/layer-definitions.ts, lib/map/floorLabelIcons.ts, lib/preview/viewerBuildings.ts (new), PreviewOverlay.tsx, store/mapStore/buildingsSlice.ts, plus 8 new tests.

pnpm test · pnpm lint · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Browser-checked: inside gothru the neighbour renders as a labelled slate shell; clicking it enters that building and gothru becomes the shell.

issues.display_title: Issue #609: Preview/live: cross-building directions render both endpoint buildings indoors
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Direction origin/destination search already spans every floor of every building — directionAreaOptions in PreviewOverlay.tsx:155 walks canvasData.levels with no building filter, so R35/R36 are already met. What is missing is the display: exactly one building can be indoors at a time, so picking a destination in another building leaves the viewer looking at one endpoint with the other one invisible.

useFloorPlanLayer renders visibleLevelIds ?? levelsAtOrBelow(canvasData, activeLevelId) (src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts:186), and levelsAtOrBelow is scoped to the active level's building group. There is no concept of a second indoor building.

Scope

  • Track routeBuildingIds: the buildings owning the route's origin and destination endpoints, resolved from each endpoint's levelId (a level with no buildingId belongs to the first building record — the levelsInBuilding rule in src/lib/editor/levels.ts:114).
  • While a route is active, both endpoint buildings render indoors even though only one is selected (R22, R39). Every other building stays a shell (R40) — this consumes the indoor-building set introduced by the context-shell task.
  • In direction mode, hovering or focusing an outer shell temporarily renders that building indoors; ending hover/focus returns it to a shell unless it is selected or on the route (R23, R24).
  • Cleanup (PRD §11): closing direction mode clears routeBuildingIds and any hover/focus preview; changing the route clears the temporary preview; the selected building does not move on its own.
  • Route path stays honest. planMultiLevelRoute (src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:96) connects two levels only through a shared accessId connector group and has no building concept at all. Two buildings share no connector, so a cross-building pair resolves to missing-destination-connector — which is the existing failure state R42 asks for. This task renders the indoor context at both ends and surfaces that state; it must not invent a path. R41 explicitly rules out an outdoor walking segment in this version.

Out of scope

Outdoor walking paths between buildings, any change to the routing engine's connector model, and editing cross-building connectors from the viewer.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A route whose endpoints are in two buildings renders both buildings indoors while it is active
  • Buildings not selected and not on the route stay shells during a cross-building route
  • Hovering or focusing an outer shell in direction mode renders it indoors temporarily
  • Ending hover/focus returns that building to a shell unless selected or on the route
  • Closing direction mode clears route buildings and the hover/focus preview
  • A cross-building pair with no resolvable route shows the existing failure state — no invented path
  • Same-building single-floor and multi-floor routes behave exactly as they do today
  • Unit tests: endpoint → building resolution, the indoor-building set under route/hover/selection, and cleanup on close
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Refs

PRD: #590 — docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-07-overview-recenter-map/prd.md on branch product-docs (R22–R24, R35–R42).
Depends on the context-shell indoor/outer building split.

RESULT

Shipped in 99388e2, merged to development via #614 as 20eb6c2.

Direction origin/destination search already spanned every building (#313 + #564), so this task was display only. The render model now takes the route's endpoint buildings and the direction-mode hover preview alongside the selected building. Both are derived rather than stored, which is what closes PRD §11: closing direction mode or changing endpoints empties them with no reset step, and the preview clears on route change.

Two things the straightforward implementation gets wrong, both fixed here:

  1. Hover cannot be a hit on the massing layer. Previewing a building removes its shell, which drops the hover, restores the shell, and flickers forever. Hover is resolved from the cursor's position via buildingIdAtLngLat instead — unaffected by what is currently drawn.
  2. A second indoor building rendered as a ghost. Levels that are not the active one draw at 0.25 opacity as below-the-active reference. The first cut made the shell vanish and put nothing visible in its place. canvasDataToGeoJson now accepts extra active levels: a route endpoint contributes its own floor, a hover preview its building's entry floor.

The route line is untouched and stays honest. planMultiLevelRoute connects levels only through a shared accessId group, so a cross-building pair resolves to missing-destination-connector — the existing failure state R42 asks for. R41 rules out an outdoor walking segment in this version and a test pins that nothing invents one.

Files: lib/preview/viewerBuildings.ts, lib/map/geojson-utils.ts, lib/map/useFloorPlanLayer.ts, PreviewOverlay.tsx, plus 8 new tests.

pnpm test · pnpm lint · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

One AC could not be closed in the browser: a route with both endpoints set across buildings. The sample project has only one direction-eligible object, so no such pair can be built there. Hover preview and the destination-side case were verified visually; endpoint → building resolution and the no-invented-path status are covered by unit tests.

issues.display_title: Issue #610: Preview/live: recenter button that fits all buildings without forcing Overview
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Preview and live have no recenter control. A viewer who pans or zooms away has no way back to the whole project — the only fit-all is the one-shot fitBounds on mount (PreviewOverlay.tsx:375, guarded by didFit). The editor's recenter lives in EditorCanvasZoom.tsx and operates on the 2D canvas, not the map.

The bounds helper already exists and is per-building-placement aware: getBuildingLngLatBounds (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts, #571).

Scope

  • A recenter button near the existing zoom/tilt controls in preview and live — the bottom-right stack next to MapTiltControl (PreviewOverlay.tsx:539). Same button chrome as its neighbours, with an accessible label.
  • Clicking it fits every building in the viewport via getBuildingLngLatBounds, preserving the current pitch/bearing.
  • Recenter must not change the mode. Fitting a multi-building site zooms out past OUTDOOR_ENTER_ZOOM (16.25), and useAutoOutdoor watches the raw zoom event — so a naive fitBounds flips an indoor viewer into Overview, exactly what R51 forbids. The camera move must be excluded from the auto-overview rule (a suppression flag around the programmatic move, cleared when it ends). Watch moveend, not a timer: an interrupted or replaced animation must not leave the flag stuck on.
  • Recenter does not change the selected building (R52) and keeps Overview selected when already in Overview (R53).
  • Viewer-only: no editor or placement control may be exposed alongside it (R54).

Out of scope

Overview dropdown, context shells, cross-building directions. Changing the auto-overview thresholds themselves.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Recenter button appears near the zoom controls in preview and in live
  • Clicking it fits all buildings in the viewport
  • Recentering while inside a building does not switch to Overview and does not change the selected building
  • Recentering while in Overview stays in Overview
  • Manual zoom-out still switches to Overview afterwards — the suppression does not leak past the animation
  • Works on a single-building project
  • Unit tests: the suppression rule (programmatic move vs user zoom) against the existing nextOutdoorState hysteresis
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Refs

PRD: #590 — docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-07-overview-recenter-map/prd.md on branch product-docs (R45, R48–R54).
Existing helpers: getBuildingLngLatBounds (#571), useAutoOutdoor (#549).

RESULT

Shipped in 0018788, merged to development via #615 as 952d2d3.

The button is a maplibre IControl, so it lands in the same top-right stack as the zoom buttons and stays with them rather than being an absolutely-positioned element that has to be kept in sync. Clicking it fits every building through getBuildingLngLatBounds, keeping the current pitch and bearing.

The camera move was never the hard part — the mode was. The zoom watcher owns the mode, and fitting a multi-building site normally crosses the outdoor threshold, so a plain fitBounds drops an indoor viewer into Overview (R51). The move runs inside keepModeThrough, which suppresses the watcher until the camera settles and releases on moveend or idle, whichever comes first: an interrupted or replaced animation cannot leave the flag stuck on, and neither can a call whose move never starts.

Files: lib/map/recenterControl.ts (new), lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts, PreviewOverlay.tsx, plus 5 new tests driving the real hook rather than a copy of its rule.

pnpm test · pnpm lint · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Browser: the control appears under the zoom buttons; recentering from Overview keeps Overview, and recentering inside a building keeps the building and its floor. Worth noting the sample project's fit lands near zoom 18 — above the 16.25 threshold — so that run does not exercise the suppression itself. The unit tests do, with a site-scale fit.

Follow-up 705b020 (#617). Two defects the screenshot pass exposed:

  1. The Search/Direction panel wrapper spans the full width and was opaque to pointer events across that strip, so with either panel open the zoom, 3D and recenter buttons could not be clicked. Pre-existing for the other two; recenter sits squarely in the band. The wrapper is now click-through.
  2. Recenter flattened a tilted view — fitBounds frames bounds with the camera upright. It now uses cameraForBounds + easeTo and preserves pitch and bearing.
